fieldValues.title: A Field's id travels in the outputs clients already receive
fieldValues.decision_rationale: `rfc-decision-b2ff7c91` requires identity in machine-facing outputs, and one mechanism beats two (Conformance: one way over many). A separate read would add a second way to the same goal and leave each client calling once per Type and combining results. The reversal of RFC-039's retirement of the keyword is explicit and named, which axis 5-11's boundary clause requires of a renewal. Records stay keyed by `Field.name`.
fieldValues.decision_statement: An implementation reports each Field's id beside its name in the authoring projection, as the annotation keyword `x-srs-field-id`, so no client needs a separate read to learn it.
fieldValues.decision_scope: The authoring projection in every implementation. Not the validation projection, the RFC-035 emitter, stored Records, or any other `x-srs-*` keyword.
fieldValues.alternatives_considered: Do nothing: clients see names only, and `b2ff7c91` stays unmet in these outputs. A separate `(typeId, typeVersion, name) -> fieldId` read plus facets listing contributing Types: the schema stays free of the keyword, closest to RFC-039, at the cost of a second mechanism and one call per Type per view. In-place ids now with that read added later as a convenience: still open, and adding it needs a new decision.
fieldValues.accepted_costs: About 58 bytes per schema property. Every implementation must report ids. `x-srs-field-id` becomes the first `x-srs-*` keyword registered outside the validation projection, so srs#366's later registry inherits its name and placement, and removing it would need a supersession. This settles in practice that the authoring projection serves SRS-aware clients while the validation projection stays plain.
evidence_refs: the-greenman/srs-web#547 (D6 follow-up: 'Ask the engine for field ids')
fieldValues.review_trigger:
1. Agents keep reading a schema or running a find only to learn one field's id. *Checked at:* srs-context friction records and the first MCP use after implementation; then add the Record-only read.
2. A third-party consumer cannot take the keyword, for example under strict schema validation. *Checked at:* srs#366, when it leaves parked.
3. srs#366 rules on keyword placement in a way this keyword contradicts. *Checked at:* srs#366.
*Done its job:* srs-web restores "Tell apart by" with no client matching on names.
